schools.name: DeWitt

colors.names: Blue and gold (names per Wikipedia; hex values approximate)

schools.class_current: Division 1 (MaxPreps lists D1 every season 2018-19 to 2025-26; Division 1 in 2024 and 2026 district play)

state_runner_ups.coach: Ron Marlan (1st year as head coach)
state_runner_ups.notes: Program's first state final. Regular season 13-7, 3rd in CAAC Division 3. Beat Haslett 57-44 in the district final. Won the regional final over Essexville Garber 63-46, the first regional title since 1997. Beat Flint Powers Catholic 56-49 in the quarterfinal and Muskegon Heights 59-55 (OT) in the semifinal.

final_fours.result: Semifinal: lost 40-43 (OT) to East Grand Rapids at Breslin Center. Finished 26-1 under coach Jim Lutzke, the school record for wins, and set a 26-game school win streak.
Semifinal: lost 62-70 to Detroit Country Day (ranked No. 1). Quarterfinal: beat Petoskey 71-65. Coach Jim Lutzke. The senior class went 51-3 over two seasons.

notable_players.name: Erik Kangas
notable_players.accolades: Starter on the 2003-04 Class B runner-up. Listed in the MHSAA record book for 83 three-pointers in a season (205 attempts) and .907 free-throw percentage (88 of 97), both in 2003-04. The MHSAA record book spells his name 'Eric'; the DeWitt Hall of Fame roster spells it 'Erik'.

notable_coaches.name: Jim Lutzke
notable_coaches.notes: Coached the 1994-95 team (26-1, first regional title, first undefeated regular season) and the 1995-96 team. Both teams reached the Class B Final Four and are in the DeWitt Athletic Hall of Fame. He was also DeWitt's athletic director in 1994.

notable_coaches.name: Ron Marlan
notable_coaches.years: 2003-04 (1st year); MaxPreps lists him for 2005-06 to 2007-08 and 2011-12
notable_coaches.notes: Coached the 2003-04 team to the program's only state final (Class B runner-up). The 2007-08 team went 19-3 and 10-0 in the CAAC Gold.

notable_coaches.name: Bill Flannery
notable_coaches.notes: His 2018-19 team went 21-4 and 13-2 in the CAAC Blue.

notable_coaches.name: Bill McCullen
notable_coaches.notes: Assistant coach on both Final Four teams. Best known as DeWitt's longtime girls basketball head coach (from 1996; 500+ wins). Inducted into the BCAM Hall of Fame in 2024.

uncertain: The 1995-96 season record is not stated directly. The Hall of Fame gives 51-3 over two seasons, which together with 26-1 in 1994-95 implies 25-2, but that figure is derived, not sourced.
michigan-football.com's all-time tournament page lists an unlabeled footer 'D18:R6:S0' (likely 18 district and 6 regional titles), but it does not define these labels.

Other quarterfinal appearances (not Final Four): 1951-52 Class D (lost 27-74 to Fowler), 1952-53 Class D (lost 36-56 to Detroit All Saints), and 1996-97 Class B (lost 78-86 in OT to Flint Powers Catholic). Source: https://www.mhsaa.com/sites/default/files/Media/boysbasketballfinals.pdf
No individual DeWitt boys players with college or pro careers were verified; the RealGM DeWitt page could not be fetched. Trey McKenney is NOT a DeWitt alum (he attended Orchard Lake St. Mary's).

notable_players.college: Western Michigan (redshirt), then Lake Superior State (2017-18 to 2020-21)

notable_players.name: Tom Coss
notable_players.accolades: Starting point guard on two Mason teams that went 39-5 combined, including a 21-1 team in the Mason Hall of Fame. Averaged 7.9 points and 4.1 assists as a senior. Later taught and coached for 37 years, 31 of them at Mason.

notable_players.name: Craig Webster
notable_players.accolades: Two-time All-Circuit and All-Area basketball player. Led the Capital Circuit in scoring as a junior; the team went 16-5 his senior year.

notable_players.name: Dan DeMartin
notable_players.accolades: All-League; All-State as a senior. Longtime assistant coach in boys and girls basketball.
notable_players.college: Lansing Community College; Northeast Missouri State (now Truman State)

notable_coaches.name: Lee Chaney
notable_coaches.notes: 2022-23 (21-3) and 2023-24 (20-3) teams both went 10-0 in the CAAC Red; 2011-12 team went 19-3.

uncertain: No state final or semifinal appearances found. Quarterfinal appearances: 1960-61 Class B (lost 42-57 to Holland Christian) and 1961-62 Class B (beat Albion 72-39 in the regional final, then lost 50-73 to East Grand Rapids). Source: https://michigan-football.com/bb/mason.htm

schools.name: St. Johns

colors.names: Red and black (names per Wikipedia; hex values approximate)

schools.class_current: UNCERTAIN. Division 1 in the Feb 2024 district assignments (Grand Ledge district), but MaxPreps lists St. Johns baseball in Division 2 for 2025-26. Divisions are assigned per sport, so verify the current boys basketball division.

final_fours.result: Semifinal: lost 48-57 to Holland Christian at Jenison Field House. Beat Flint Kearsley 47-43 in the regional final and Utica 50-48 in the quarterfinal. Finished 17-3 and won the West Central League (7-1). Coach Dwane Wirick. The school calls it the only St. Johns boys team to reach the state semifinals.

notable_players.name: Douglas Knight
notable_players.accolades: Team captain; All-Conference twice and All-State three times. Set the school single-game record of 31 points in 1952. Member of the 1953-54 semifinal team. St. Johns Hall of Fame 2022.

notable_players.name: Levi Rost
notable_players.accolades: Basketball standout. Junior-college All-American at Lansing CC. 2005 All-MAC Second Team at Western Michigan, where he set a school record with nine 3-pointers in one game (at Buffalo). St. Johns Hall of Fame 2016.
notable_players.pro: Played professionally in Europe for 10 seasons (per the St. Johns HOF; the school alumni page says Spain)

notable_players.name: Keith Haske
notable_players.accolades: All-Conference and captain in basketball, football and baseball

notable_coaches.name: Dwane Wirick
notable_coaches.notes: Coached the only St. Johns boys team to reach the state semifinals (17-3; won the West Central League, district and regional).

notable_coaches.name: Keith Haske
notable_coaches.notes: St. Johns alum (1976). As varsity coach his teams won six league titles and went 164-114. Also coached at Charlevoix and Traverse City St. Francis (600+ career wins). BCAM Hall of Fame 2014.

state_titles.notes: The program's only title under the Lansing Catholic (Central) name. Beat Detroit Community 56-47 in the quarterfinal and Menominee 64-39 in the semifinal at Breslin Center.
Won as Lansing St. Mary, a predecessor school (see uncertain). St. Mary's first MHSAA title. Captain Herb Brogan scored 16 in the final. Beat Charlevoix 38-28 in the semifinal.
Won as Lansing St. Mary; second straight title. Bob Wines scored 15 in the final. Beat Dundee 38-25 in the quarterfinal.
Won as Lansing St. Mary. Beat Blissfield 34-33 (OT) in the quarterfinal.
Won as Lansing St. Mary. Beat Detroit St. Cecilia 34-24 in the quarterfinal. Score discrepancy: the past-champions list says 50-33, but the finals PDF row for Cass City reads 23-50.
Won as Lansing St. Mary. Team inducted into the Greater Lansing Sports Hall of Fame (1989).

Semifinal: lost 51-59 to Detroit St. Martin dePorres (the eventual champion); beat Newaygo 47-43 in the quarterfinal

uncertain: Lineage: St. Mary High School (founded 1900) closed in 1963, along with Resurrection. Its students went to the new Gabriels and O'Rafferty high schools, which merged in 1970 as Lansing Catholic Central, later renamed Lansing Catholic (Wikipedia). MHSAA lists the Lansing St. Mary titles under 'Lansing St. Mary', and michigan-football.com's Lansing Catholic Central page does not include St. Mary results. Decide whether to credit St. Mary's 5 titles to Lansing Catholic or show them as predecessor history. Wikipedia's school page lists only 2008 as a boys basketball title.
Title-season records (win-loss) were not found for any Lansing Catholic or St. Mary championship team.
1944 final score: 50-33 (past-champions list) vs. 23-50 (finals PDF Cass City row).

Grad years for the record-book players are not stated (only career spans), so they were left blank. Austin Nichols's 2007-09 career span suggests he played on the 2008 title team, but no source confirms it.
Lansing Gabriels results (1963-70, e.g., the 1970 Class B regional final win over St. Johns) were not researched as part of the lineage.

meta.notes: Season format follows MHSAA tournament year minus one (e.g., MHSAA '2008' = 2007-08). michigan-football.com is a fan-compiled tournament database; its results match the MHSAA finals PDF wherever both were checked.
